test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Feb, 2026 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In a certain examination, 67% of the candidates successfully passed, while 165 candidates failed. Determine the total number of candidates who appeared for the examination.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Percentage = 100%

Failed Percentage = 100% − 67% = 33%

According to the question, 33% = 165

Total Candidates (100%) = (165 ÷ 33) × 100 = 5 × 100 = 500

**∴ The correct answer is 500 candidates.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage of candidates passed = 67%

Number of candidates failed = 165

**Formula Used:**

Total Candidates = (Number of Failures ÷ Percentage of Failures) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/07babff4babd548e10cf4db7197e6202a038a7147fa7596b568ef47c3bd10a6f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total number of candidates be x.

⇒ Percentage of failed candidates = 100% − 67% = 33%

⇒ Number of failed candidates = 33% of x = 165

⇒ (33 ÷ 100) × x = 165

⇒ x = (165 × 100) ÷ 33

⇒ x = 5 × 100 = 500

**∴ The correct answer is 500 candidates.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Base Rule

In any population or set, the total quantity is always considered as 100%. The sum of all individual percentage components must equal 100%.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

To convert a fraction to a percentage, multiply by 100. Example: 1/4 = (1/4 × 100)% = 25%.

Successive Percentage Change

If a value is changed by a% and then by b%, the net change is [a + b + (ab ÷ 100)]%.
